links.outcome: Neonatal outcomes and perceived safety with remote nurse AI-assisted fetal surveillance
links.effect: Cooling 6 (0.25%) pre vs 2 (0.08%) during trial, p = .10; no significant differences in neonatal outcomes; 78.8% of responding nurses said OB HUB improved safety.
links.quote: There were no significant differences between groups for neonatal outcomes.

links.outcome: Neonatal cooling and other neonatal outcomes following remote nurse surveillance
links.effect: Bundled AI-assisted remote nurse surveillance: cooling occurred in 6 births (0.25%) before implementation versus 2 (0.08%) during the trial (p = .10). No significant differences were reported for neonatal outcomes.
links.quote: Six births (0.25%) resulted in cooling prior to implementation and 2 (0.08%) cooling events occurred during the trial; these differences were not significant (p = .10).

links.effect: Cooling occurred in 0.25% of pre-implementation births and 0.08% of trial births, which was not statistically significant.
links.quote: Six births (0.25%) resulted in cooling prior to implementation and 2 (0.08%) cooling events occurred during the trial; these differences were not significant (p = .10).

links.effect: Average perceived safety remained unchanged between periods, although 78.8% of responding nurses indicated the system improved safety.
links.quote: Average level of safety perceived by nurses and providers remained relatively unchanged when comparing pre- and postimplementation survey results; however, of those responding, 78.8% of nurses indicated the OB HUB improved safety.

links.effect: No significant differences between groups for neonatal outcomes were observed.
links.quote: There were no significant differences between groups for neonatal outcomes.
